quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: You must drive with extra caution near a pedestrian using a white cane because:
questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog means the pedestrian is blind. Slow down, give them the right-of-way, and be ready to stop to prevent injury or danger.

questions.question: When you are in traffic crossing a railroad track with no signals or gates:

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
You may pass slower drivers while crossing the track.
Make sure your vehicle can cross the entire track without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your vehicle can cross the entire track without stopping.
questions.explanation: Before driving onto the tracks, check that you have enough space to cross completely. Never pass another vehicle at a railroad crossing. Always look for trains before crossing any tracks.

questions.question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road:

options.text: Should yield to drivers already on the public road.
May force their way into traffic.
Can assume that other drivers will change lanes to make room.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should yield to drivers already on the public road.
questions.explanation: When entering traffic from a driveway or private road, you must yield to drivers already on the public road. Merge safely when it is possible to do so.

questions.question: You are driving at night and another vehicle is approaching from the opposite direction. Your headlights should:

options.text: Be off. Use parking lights instead.
Be on either high or low beam.

questions.explanation: Do not use high beam headlights when another vehicle is approaching or when you are following another vehicle at night. Use low beam to keep everyone safe.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic signal at an intersection has the same requirements as:
questions.explanation: A flashing red signal means you must stop completely and yield to all traffic that does not have to stop.

questions.question: Do not pass:

options.text: When school bus lights are flashing.

questions.explanation: Never pass if an oncoming vehicle is in the passing lane, your view is blocked by a curve or hill, at an intersection, before or on railroad crossings, on bridges, or in no passing zones. Do not pass a stopped school bus with flashing red lights unless you are on the opposite side of a multilane road with a median or shared turn lane.

questions.question: To safely pass a bicycle, you should:

options.text: Honk at the bicyclist to let them know you're passing.
Drive in the bicycle lane until you get a chance to pass.
Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
Rush ahead to pull in front of the bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and give them as much space as possible.
questions.explanation: Slow down and give bicyclists as much space as you can. Bicyclists have less protection than drivers and should not be crowded. Passing too quickly can force them off course.

questions.question: Highway signs that require drivers to obey an instruction are called:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must do. Breaking these rules can result in a penalty.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Keep to the side indicated by the arrow.
You may drive in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep to the side indicated by the arrow.
questions.explanation: This "Keep right" sign tells you that a traffic island, median, or barrier is ahead. You must stay to the right of it.

questions.question: Your vehicle hits an unattended parked car and you cannot find the owner. You must:

options.text: Leave because you have done all you can.
Leave a written note with your name, address, and details of what happened.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a written note with your name, address, and details of what happened.
questions.explanation: Stop and try to find the vehicle's owner. If you cannot find them, leave a written note that includes your name, your address, and what happened in the accident.

questions.question: If you cannot merge safely, you must stop when yielding the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: When you yield the right-of-way, you must stop if you cannot safely merge into traffic.

questions.question: Drivers cannot pass from either side of a ____ centerline.
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means no traffic from either direction can cross it to pass.

questions.question: When entering a street from a driveway, you:

options.text: Must drive slowly to give approaching vehicles and pedestrians time to move.
Must honk your horn so approaching vehicles and pedestrians know to move.
Must stop and only proceed when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
Can ignore pedestrians if there is no sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop and only proceed when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
questions.explanation: Always stop before entering the roadway from a driveway. Yield to any approaching vehicles or pedestrians. This is required by law.

questions.question: Worn or bald tires:
questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires increase stopping distance, make turning harder, and increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: This sign warns you that:

options.text: Trucks are not allowed on an upcoming hill.
Trucks are on an upcoming hill.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that a steep hill or downgrade is ahead.

questions.question: If a driver sees an animal on the roadway:

options.text: Pass the animal as closely as possible.

questions.explanation: Be very cautious when you see an animal on the roadway. Pass it slowly to avoid startling it.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should not:

options.text: Check your side and rearview mirrors.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
Use your cell phone to call police to check if the road ahead is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your cell phone to call police to check if the road ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors, use your turn signal, and look for other drivers. Do not use your cell phone to check road conditions.

questions.question: A red traffic light means you must:
questions.explanation: At a red light, you must stop at the stop line, before any crosswalk, and before entering the intersection.

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes mean?

options.text: Drivers may pass, even if it could be dangerous.
Drivers may pass if it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: White dashed lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. You may cross them to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: Highways and roads freeze before ramps and bridges.
questions.explanation: Ramps and bridges freeze before regular roads because they are in the air with cold air underneath. Drive slowly on bridges in freezing weather.

questions.question: When making a turn, you must ____ your speed.
questions.explanation: Slow down before turning. This helps you stay in your lane, keep control of your vehicle, and react to surprises.

questions.question: When driving in rain, you must:
questions.explanation: In rain, use your low beam headlights to see and be seen.

questions.question: The traffic light turns yellow as you approach an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to cross before the red light.
Be ready to stop in the middle of the intersection.
Be ready to stop before you reach the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop before you reach the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means the red light is coming soon. Get ready to stop before the intersection if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: An inattentive driver is someone who:

options.text: Looks away from the road or daydreams.
Only watches the car in front.

questions.explanation: Stay focused while driving. Do not look at passengers, search for items, read, sightsee, or daydream. Keep watching the road, checking mirrors, and checking your instruments regularly. These habits keep you alert.

questions.question: Your blind spot is the area:

options.text: You cannot see without turning your head.
You can see in your rearview mirror.
You can see in your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see without turning your head.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas you cannot see without turning your head. They are usually to the sides and behind your vehicle.
